origin.description: Multiplies y by a power of the shrinkage correlation without forming the power.
origin.usage: crossprod.powcor.shrink(x, y, alpha, lambda, w, verbose=TRUE)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A data matrix, one observation per row.

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: A matrix with one row per column of x.

arguments.name: lambda
arguments.text: Correlation shrinkage intensity from 0 to 1. Omitted means estimate it. In Python the name is lambda_value.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: One weight per row. Omitted means equal weights that sum to 1.

arguments.name: verbose
arguments.text: Print the intensity. The default is true.

origin.details: Unlike powcor.shrink, exponent 1 still uses the singular-value path. Zero-variance rows of the product are replaced by the same rows of y.
origin.value: A matrix with one row per column of x.
origin.example:
Y <- cbind(c(1, 0, 1, 0.5), c(0, 1, -1, 0.5))
as.numeric(crossprod.powcor.shrink(X, Y, alpha=0.5, verbose=FALSE))
